answer: Interleaved Proof Windows anchors each identity's first action to a randomized slot derived from a shared clock. An agent gets one submission per window; a second entry inside that window is dropped and its credential flagged for the next cycle, so a fleet must either stagger across many windows or lose entries. Enrollment costs a fixed opal credit per slot, meaning N identities pay N credits plus forfeited slots during ramp-up. Each successful slot also logs a jetty timestamp that future windows check, so cloning faster than the clock yields nothing.
